name: Dubuffet cells
description: Abstract cell drawings like a hand-drawn floor plan: the whole surface broken into cells with mostly straight edges and rounded corners, nested two or three levels inside one another, thick black outlines. Each cell is straight parallel red or blue stripes, plain brushy white, or a small solid colour patch. Purely abstract, no faces, figures or objects.
light: no light source, flat colour on white
white cells and black outlines on a black ground
muted earth tones: pink, grey and ochre cells on beige paper
bright red, blue and black hatching on pure white
composition: all-over cells to every edge, nested 2-3 levels deep, many small cells packed around a few large ones, no ground or horizon
one big irregular cluster of cells, isolated on plain ground
a dense maze of cells in loose bands, like a map of an imaginary city seen from above
loose looping lines over a dark ground, cells half formed
camera_or_medium: marker, felt pen and vinyl paint on paper or panel; flat, confident black contour
texture_detail: straight parallel hand-drawn stripes with wide gaps and white showing between them, one direction per cell, in red or blue; thick black outlines, often with a thin red dashed line running inside them; white fills show brush strokes; fills roughly 40% striped, 40% white, 20% small solid patches (red, blue, pale blue, grey, black); slight hand wobble
avoid: jigsaw puzzle pieces, tabs and sockets
subjects: an endless hand-drawn floor plan of nested striped and white cells
a single floating cluster of lumpy cells
bands of red and blue hatched cells like a striped map
looping black contours half closing into cells on a dark ground
